title: Naval on late-stage funding: keep control, hire slowly, treat early employees as founders
summary: Naval explains how founders of hot late-stage companies can raise money without surrendering control, why raising less keeps companies faster, and how to vet investors. He also covers hiring discipline, early founder liquidity, and giving early employees founder-level equity.

principles.text: Never give up control; valuation is temporary but control is permanent.
principles.quote: “Valuation is temporary. Control is forever.” Whoever has control can effectively end up controlling your valuation later. Never give up control.

principles.text: With multiple bidders, sell common stock, or common plus liquidation preference, and skip the protective provisions.
principles.quote: If I had a high-growth, high-performance company with multiple bidders— and obviously these kinds of negotiations are only possible when there are multiple bidders—I would be selling common stock.

principles.text: More cash makes companies spend more and move slower; some cash constraint helps.
principles.quote: when you raise more money you do spend more money. There’s just no way around that, no matter how disciplined you are.

principles.text: Unbundle venture capital into advice, control and money, and take only what you need from each source.
principles.quote: venture capital is a bundle—it’s a bundle of advice, control, and money. The more options you have, the more you can unbundle those three things

principles.text: Judge investors by how they behave in the term sheet process; walk away early if signals are bad.
principles.quote: You can learn everything you need to know about a VC during the term sheet process before the close. And don’t be afraid to call off the close if you’re getting negative signals.

principles.text: Hire extremely slowly, only for a burning need, and trim ruthlessly.
principles.quote: I think you should hire extremely slowly. Hire only after there’s a burning need for that person. I think you have to be ruthless about firing and trimming the ranks.
